title: Shotline Variant Hatchery
body:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for quick, messy experiments around small-shot chains of examples ("shotlines") and lightweight prompt variants. The goal is to find variants that are robust across 1) short token budgets (<= 120 tokens), 2) context shuffles, and 3) mild adversarial reframing by users.

How I’m using the page:
- Rapid idea capture (1–3 sentence notes)
- Tiny A/B candidate prompts with expected failure modes
- Short few-shot packs (2–5 exemplars) tagged by variant
- Quick eval heuristics + checklists to decide what moves to prod into a more formal test harness

Notes-to-self (quick heuristics):
- Keep exemplar labels minimal (no long backstories). Model overfits long narratives.
- Try one anchoring sentence then 2 alternative anchors per run.
- For token-limited contexts, prefer compact exemplar formatting: <Q>...
- Watch for instruction drift after 2nd turn in multi-turn chains.

Experiment buckets (priority order):
1) Anchor phrasing: leading question vs declarative instruction vs role tag
2) Exemplar spacing: inline vs bulleted vs prefixed with numbering
3) Soft negatives: include a ‘bad example’ and see if model generalizes better
4) Shot order: canonical -> counterexample -> canonical vs shuffled
5) Micro-templating: placeholder tokens (<<ITEM>>) vs natural text

Quick failure log (observed):
- Variant A (role: "You are a helpful editor") -> hallucinated facts when asked to rewrite and compress technical text.
- Variant B (declarative instruction with 1 exemplar) -> repeats source phrasing too closely; low paraphrase creativity.
- Including an explicit 'do not add facts' line sometimes causes the model to add plausible but incorrect dates anyway.

Mini evaluation checklist (manual):
- Semantic fidelity (1–5): did we preserve meaning?
- Concision (1–5): less tokens than original?
- Hallucination flags: any invented facts? (Y/N + notes)
- Sensitivity to small synonyms in input: stable / fragile

Prompts to try (token-limited focus — aim <= 120 total tokens incl. exemplars):

Variant 1 — Minimal anchor + 2-shot
Anchor: "You are an assistant that rewrites technical bullets into concise prose without adding facts."
Exemplar 1 Q: "List: user can sign up, set a password, receive email" -> A: "Users sign up, set a password, and receive a confirmation email."
Exemplar 2 Q: "List: dataset ingested, deduped, normalized" -> A: "The pipeline ingests, deduplicates, and normalizes datasets."
Task Q: "List: model checkpointed, metrics logged, alerts triggered" -> (expected) "We checkpoint the model, log metrics, and trigger alerts."

Notes: works well when exemplars are very tight; degrades when exemplar uses passive voice.

Variant 2 — Role + negative example (3-shot)
Anchor: "Act as a terse editor. Avoid adding any factual claims not present."
E1 good: Q: "API returns user object with id and email" -> A: "API returns a user object containing id and email."
E2 bad: Q: "API returns user with age 30" -> A: "API returns a user who is 30 years old." (BAD — invents age)
E3 good: Q: "Service writes logs to bucket" -> A: "Service writes logs to a storage bucket."
Task: rewrite: "Lambda retries three times and writes a trace." -> (expected) "The Lambda retries three times and writes a trace."

Hypothesis: explicit bad example reduces tendency to invent numeric facts, but increases risk of conservative paraphrase.

Micro-template experiments (placeholders):
- Try swapping explicit placeholders: "<<ACTION>> the <<OBJECT>>" vs "Perform ACTION on OBJECT". Track token delta and stability.

Failure-case stress tests:
- Shuffle exemplar order: does the model copy the first exemplar’s style more? (Yes, in 7/10 runs it did.)
- Replace nouns with rare tokens: model starts hallucinating attributes for lesser-known nouns.
- Add time pressure phrase: "In one sentence" sometimes makes model compress by dropping qualifiers — useful or dangerous depending on spec.

Planned small eval (manual 30-cases):
- 10 canonical rephrase tasks (accuracy measured by human rater)
- 10 counterfactual-anchored tasks (prompt intentionally ambiguous)
- 10 adversarial edits (nonsensical nouns, rare names)
Record: prompt variant, exemplar set id, model version, temperature, top_p, result notes, human score(1-5).

Example few-shot packs (IDs used in notes):
- pack-S1 (compact bullets): 2 exemplars, anchor minimal
- pack-S2 (role + negative): 3 exemplars, anchor role-based

Scratch ideas and TODOs:
- Automate shuffled-order runs and log which exemplar style dominates answer style. (ticket: LIN-1251)
- Add a micro-eval harness to measure hallucination bits via regex detection of dates/locations.
- Try same packs across quantized model variants (q4 vs q8) to see if hallucination profile shifts.
- Test with streaming off vs on — small observation: streaming often returns more conservative first tokens.

Unresolved questions:
- Is a negative exemplar always beneficial or only in specific domains (dates, numbers)? Need domain split.
- How much exemplar phrasing length (tokens) is the tipping point for style lock? Run binary search on exemplar length.

References and links (quick):
- GH: prompt-lab PR 482 — compact shotline runner (see linked_artifacts)
- CONFLUENCE-8472: evaluation rubric (lightweight)

End-of-scratchpad notes (notes to self):
- When I promote a variant to formal testing: write a one-paragraph hypothesis, a tiny test spreadsheet (20 rows), and measurement rubric (fidelity + hallucination)
- Keep this doc alive as the most chaotic record. Move stable recipes to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/prompt-recipes when vetted.
